The short version

Own IBKR for three to ten years. The business is a brokerage tollbooth: commissions and related fees on a growing global account base, with an API surface that still looks like the natural home for serious automated investing. The fear that price competition and agentic brokers hollow out the toll is the mispricing to watch — not a one-quarter soft print on net interest. What would change the view first is a sustained break in the fee toll (commission dollars falling while accounts keep rising, or $/order collapsing without a volume explanation). Second is clear loss of the agentic API lane — share we cannot yet measure, so design-wins and execute-native MCP posture are the live proxy. Third, and secondary, is a multi-quarter stall in the international franchise. NII and market-making stay in the archive footnote. They are not the hero.

IBKR Desk · Latent capital · pack 2026-09-21 · letter refresh 2026-09-27 · as of Q2’26 (period end 2026-06-30)

Interactive Brokers is not a retail meme shop waiting for zero commissions to erase it. It clears and carries trades for a large, increasingly global client base, charges a toll on that activity, and runs one of the deepest public brokerage APIs in the industry. The stock still often prices as if the toll were fragile and as if interest income were the whole story. The metrics below are the scoreboard that decides whether that fear is earned.

1. What IBKR is and how it makes money

IBKR runs a brokerage. Clients open accounts, fund them, and trade across many markets. Revenue that matters for this thesis shows up first as commissions and other fees and services — the fee toll. Net revenues and pretax income sit beside that toll as an honesty check. They are never stacked with it; they are not pieces of the same total.

In the second quarter of 2026 the company printed $673M of commissions and $87M of other fees and services, against $1,896M of net revenues and $1,456M of pretax income (~76.8% pretax margin). A year earlier commissions were $516M and other fees $62M. The toll grew. It did not thin out into a rounding error.

Together, commissions plus other fees were about 40% of net revenues that quarter. That is a mix share, not a margin claim — and it leaves room for interest and other lines without making them the story.

Inside the contract-revenue note, commissions still dominate. The Q2’26 mix was commissions $673M, market data $23M, risk exposure $25M, payment for order flow $18M, FDIC sweep $10M, and other fees $11M. Commissions are roughly 89% of that disclosed fee stack. The non-commission lines sum to $87M — the same dollars as the income-statement “other fees and services” line this quarter.

Minimum-activity fees are not printed in this series. Do not invent an API or Lite attach rate from payment for order flow or the FDIC sweep. Those are fee types, not product telemetry.

Net revenues $1,896M versus $1,480M a year earlier; pretax $1,456M versus $1,104M. Margin held in the mid-to-high 70s. That is the honesty panel next to the toll — parallel metrics, never a stack.

Archive footnote (not hero). Net interest income, NIM, and interest-earning balances are disclosed in the filings and inventoried for Product, but they are not the analytics series of record for this pack. Market-making segment history is legacy and archive. They are not promoted into the fee-toll thesis, and they are not charted.

2. Growth engine vs legacy core

Think of the stack as franchise scale on one side and toll quality on the other — sharing one brokerage.

Franchise growth — accounts, DARTs, and customer equity. These answer whether the client base and its activity are still compounding.

Toll quality — commission dollars per order and per account, fee yield on equity, and the accounts-versus-intensity split. These answer whether the toll still collects as the franchise scales.

Globality — international share of management-geography net revenues. Supportive color for the global-franchise pillar, not a substitute for the toll.

API — qualitative moat with an honest gap. Product surface is real; share metrics are blank.

Accounts: 5.185M at mid-2026 versus 3.866M a year earlier (~+34%). Customer equity: $930.3B versus $664.6B (~+40%). Equity prints are sparse before 2023 in this extract — the chart uses the dense window from early 2023.

DARTs 4.824M versus 3.552M (~+36%). Commission per cleared commissionable order: $2.64 versus $2.65 a year ago, and $3.16 at the dense-series start in early 2023. That is a gentle glide in unit price while activity scaled — not a toll collapse. Activity rose; $/order stayed in the mid-$2s.

Accounts and equity are franchise. DARTs are activity. $/order is the issuer’s own intensity print. Do not stack them.

3. Fee-toll intensity — the KPIs that prove the toll

Calculated intensity at Q2’26 (both legs present):

  • Commissions per account ≈ $129.80 (versus ≈ $133.47 a year earlier)
  • Average equity per account ≈ $179k
  • DARTs per account ≈ 0.930 (versus ≈ 0.919)
  • Quarterly fee yield on client equity ≈ 7.23 bps (simple ×4 ≈ 29 bps — labeled simple, not a trailing twelve months)

Commissions grew +30.4% nominal year over year and +26.1% in 2026-06 CPI dollars. The franchise got bigger in real terms, not just inflated ones.

Equity grew faster than commission dollars, so yield compressed even as the toll’s absolute dollars rose. Equity growth includes market moves — a caveat, not a beta attribution this cut.

The dollar split is blunt. Commissions rose +$157M year over year. Account growth contributed about +$176M; softer commissions-per-account took back about −$19M. Accounts carried the print. Intensity was a modest drag. That is an identity split, not a causal proof — but it is the right shape for a scaling franchise with a slightly easier unit take.

DARTs and accounts both move tightly with commissions in the dense window. The house intensity print remains the issuer’s $/cleared order. Trading days are not disclosed here, so there is no invented dollars-per-DART-day.

4. Globality (supportive)

Management geography for Q2’26: US net revenues $1,284M, international $612M — international about 32% of the US plus international total. Pretax: US $1,076M / international $380M.

That is management geography, not contract-revenue location. Near one-third international is supportive of the global franchise — not a stall print. Empty first-quarter geography stubs in this extract stay blank; they are not filled in.

Commission dollars by geography and Pro/Lite cohort splits remain blank. Do not dress consolidated commissions up as a regional fee toll.

5. API moat — qualitative, share still a gap

IBKR still discloses no API clients, API DARTs, or automated-order share. The quantitative pillar is unmeasured.

What is knowable: the product surface is deep (Web API, TWS/Gateway, FIX, Excel bridges; marketing claims on the order of 170 markets / 40 countries). That supports multi-asset, global, systematic strength. It does not by itself prove “agentic defaults to IBKR.”

The clearest 2026 design-win tension is MCP posture. IBKR’s official MCP is assistive — AI drafts, human reviews and submits; the FAQ says AI integrations do not automate trading. Peers (notably Alpaca, and tastytrade more recently) market execute-native agent paths. That is pressure on a narrow “agentic prefers IBKR” claim. It is not a share-based disproof, because share is still blank.

Watch for any disclosed API metric, a flip of IBKR’s MCP FAQ toward unattended execute, and peer MCP adoption — not for invented attach rates from payment for order flow.

6. Unit economics → valuation

Valuation for this pack follows the desk hierarchy, with fee-toll intensity folded into the close — not parked in an orphan dig.

  1. Toll dollars and mix — commissions / other fees / the contract-revenue stack.
  2. Intensity — commission per order, commissions per account, DARTs per account, fee yield, and the accounts-versus-intensity split.
  3. Franchise scale — accounts, equity, DARTs.
  4. Multiples — weekly trailing PE continuous; the trailing twelve-month print, the full-year print, and Street forward sit beside.
